instruction: Visit https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/searching and extract the interface components description. Save it as "ui_components.docx" on the desktop.

command: import pyautogui; import time; pyautogui.hotkey('ctrl', 's'); time.sleep(0.5);

metadata.explanation: Task requires web navigation to Apple HIG and saving UI component content. Evaluator checks file exists and has minimum word count. Similar complexity to original task.

llm_judge_reasons: Incomplete verification coverage: Instruction requires extracting 'interface components description' from a specific Apple HIG URL, but evaluator only checks file exists and has 20+ words
No content semantic verification: Metric only counts words, doesn't verify the content is actually from the specified URL or related to interface components
Missing specificity check: A document with any random 20+ words would pass (e.g., 'hello world' repeated), not necessarily the correct extracted content
Unused expected rule: 'check_file_exists: true' in expected rules is not actually used by the metric function - file existence is implicitly checked when Document(result) succeeds

Partial credit logic unclear: Metric returns word_count/min_words for documents with fewer words, but it's unclear if partial credit makes sense for this binary task (either extracted the content or didn't)
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Add content verification: Check for presence of key terms related to interface components/Apple HIG/searching (e.g., 'search field', 'interface', 'components', 'design')
Add URL verification: Include metadata or postconfig to verify the Chrome browser actually visited the required URL
Strengthen metric logic: Instead of just word count, verify document contains substantive technical content (not just repeated words)
Remove unused expected rule: Either implement check_file_exists in the metric or remove it from expected rules
Clarify scoring: For content extraction tasks, consider binary pass/fail (1.0 or 0.0) rather than partial credit based on word count
